extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on request body — Full remote code execution on the server process [verified: pickle.loads is called directly on attacker-controlled request body/query param with no restriction on unpicklable classes, enabling RCE for anyone holding the shared ops token.]

Server-side template injection via string-built Jinja2 template — Arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 SSTI sandbox escape [verified: fragment is concatenated into the Jinja2 template source string itself before render(), not passed as a render variable, enabling classic SSTI/RCE.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution on the host running the service [verified: os.system concatenates the raw host parameter with no sanitization, allowing shell metacharacter injection.]

IDOR on integrations application-status endpoint via API key — Any holder of a valid API key can read confidential status/decision/PII data for all borrowers' loan applications by iterating application_id [verified: Duplicate of finding 0 — authenticate_api_key validates only key validity, not application association, confirmed at main.py:1685-1686.]

Sensitive credential logging (Authorization header written to logs) — Credential/session-token exposure to anyone with log access, enabling session hijacking or key reuse [verified: The raw Authorization header value is logged verbatim at warning level, exposing session/API tokens to anyone with log access.]

Code injection via eval() on user-controlled expression — Potential arbitrary code execution by sandbox-escape from the restricted eval [verified: eval() on user-supplied expr with stripped __builtins__ is a well-known incomplete sandbox, allowing escape via attribute-chain tricks.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write via unsanitized 'name' parameter — Arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server filesystem, potentially leading to code execution (e.g. overwriting application source or config) [verified: name is used directly in BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name with no Path(name).name or traversal check, allowing writes outside the export directory.]
XXE in ops XML-parsing endpoint — Local file disclosure and SSRF via crafted XML external entities [verified: Same XXE-enabling parser configuration as finding 4, duplicate of the same code line.]

Staff can tamper with loan terms after underwriting decision is finalized — A support_specialist (lower-privilege staff role) can silently alter approved/rejected loan amount, term, and revenue figures without generating a new decision record, enabling fraud or bypass of underwriting controls. [verified: update_application (main.py:907-929) blocks only borrowers (by status) and underwriters (entirely) but lets support_specialist/admin PATCH financial terms on applications in any status including approved/rejected, with no new decision generated.]

Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret — If the env var is not set in a deployment, anyone can forge valid session tokens for any user/role using the known default secret [verified: SECRET_KEY falls back to a known hardcoded literal when the env var is unset, and get_current_user trusts JWTs signed with SECRET_KEY, allowing forged session tokens for any user/role if the operator forgets to set it.]

Open redirect in ops aftercard endpoint — Attacker can craft links that redirect users from the trusted domain to an arbitrary phishing site [verified: lane is passed unchecked into RedirectResponse with no allow-list or same-host validation, enabling open redirect.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read the response on behalf of a logged-in victim [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set true, permitting any origin credentialed access.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept or tamper with outbound HTTPS traffic from this endpoint [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables certificate/hostname verification for the outbound HTTPS call, enabling MITM.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Enables online brute-force/credential-stuffing against accounts and mass password-reset-token generation [verified: login and password-reset/request handlers (main.py:654-664, 682-691) contain no throttling, lockout counter, or rate-limit dependency, and no such mechanism exists elsewhere in the file.]

Password reset tokens persisted in plaintext to disk log — Account takeover for any user whose reset token leaks via the persisted log file (filesystem access, backups, log shipping). [verified: password_reset_request (main.py:686-688) writes the raw unhashed reset token to a persistent mock_log file, creating a durable plaintext account-takeover credential on disk.]

Plaintext password-reset token persisted to log file — Anyone with read access to the log file can hijack any account by using the leaked reset token before it expires. [verified: Duplicate of finding 4 — same raw_token written in cleartext via mock_log at main.py:688, confirmed persistent plaintext credential.]

Underwriter can access borrower PII outside their assigned active queue — Cross-scope PII disclosure of borrower financial and contact data to staff who should not have access to that record. [verified: get_borrower's underwriter branch (main.py:1252-1260) checks assigned_underwriter_id==user.id OR is_(None) with no status restriction, unlike application_query_for_user which also requires ACTIVE_QUEUE_STATUSES, letting underwriters view PII for draft/withdrawn/inactive applications.]

CSV formula injection in admin exports — A borrower can plant a malicious formula in a profile field (e.g. business_name) that executes as a spreadsheet formula (potential code execution or data exfiltration) when an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets. [verified: Same csv_response sink as finding 1 confirmed unsanitized; business_name originates from borrower-controlled RegisterIn/BorrowerProfileUpdateIn and flows into admin-consumed CSV exports.]

CSV formula injection in admin exports — Arbitrary formula/DDE execution in the exporting admin's spreadsheet application when the CSV is opened, potentially leading to local code execution or credential theft [verified: csv_response (main.py:1490-1500) writes attacker-influenced business_name/reasons/borrower_summary fields via DictWriter.writerows with no leading-character neutralization, confirmed across applications/decisions/documents exports.]

Session cookie Secure flag defaults to false — Session hijacking via network interception when deployed without explicitly setting COOKIE_SECURE=true [verified: secure_cookie defaults to false unless COOKIE_SECURE=true is explicitly set, so the session JWT cookie is sent over plaintext HTTP by default.]

Weak PRNG used for security-relevant code generation — Predictable codes could be brute-forced or guessed, undermining any security purpose they serve [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate a 'code' value instead of the secrets module used elsewhere, making output predictable if PRNG state is inferred.]

Internal underwriting decision reasons exposed to borrowers — Borrowers can read internal underwriter rationale attached to loan decisions, leaking confidential underwriting criteria and risk-assessment language never intended for borrower visibility. [verified: application_detail (main.py:565) includes decisions (containing internal 'reasons') unconditionally for all callers including borrowers, unlike notes/payment_accounts which are correctly gated behind is_staff(user) at lines 567-569.]

Account enumeration via registration endpoint — Attacker can determine which email addresses have registered accounts, aiding targeted phishing or credential-stuffing [verified: register() at main.py:626-628 returns a distinct 409 'Email is already registered' only when the email exists, giving a clear oracle for account enumeration.]

Document review queue leaks unassigned/inactive application data to underwriters — Information disclosure of borrower business names and pre-submission application/document status to staff outside intended scope. [verified: document_review_queue's underwriter filter (main.py:1129-1130) omits the ACTIVE_QUEUE_STATUSES check used for application viewing, exposing document/business-name/status data for out-of-scope applications.]
